title: Backward-compatible snapshot module read and VIC-II model alignment
description: An external compatibility adapter outside `native/vice` shall normalize legacy x64sc `MAINCPU` v1.2 and v1.3 modules for the pinned, unmodified VICE reader while current v1.4 modules remain byte-identical. The wrapper shall align the VIC-II model before `machine_read_snapshot` and normalize wrapper-reported `snapshot_last_error` after a successful read. No part of this compatibility path may edit, patch, generate into, or behaviorally change `native/vice`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An external compatibility adapter outside `native/vice` loads a validated `MAINCPU` v1.2 module by inserting the absent v1.3 `ane_log_level` and `lxa_log_level` fields and absent v1.4 `maincpu_jammed` field with the pinned immutable VICE defaults before `maincpu_ba_low_flags`, updates the inclusive module length, preserves every following byte and module, handles v1.3 by inserting only `maincpu_jammed`, and passes current v1.4 through byte-for-byte. Malformed or unsupported layouts fail closed. External v1.2 and v1.3 fixtures plus a current v1.4 native round-trip prove resume behavior with zero failed, zero skipped, and zero aborted prerequisites.

native/build-vice-shim.ps1 materializes the pinned VICE commit into a separate initially clean source root outside native/vice, follows the pinned VICE Team build instructions there (including required in-source build generation, explicitly approved 2026-10-08), and links only external wrapper translation units stored outside the submodule. Pre-build and post-build commit, tracked status and a complete inventory of original upstream source bytes must match exactly. Record all generated/build files separately with paths, hashes and producing commands; those artifacts are permitted only in the separate materialization/output roots and may not replace or modify original upstream source files. Any patch application, generated file or source mutation under native/vice fails the build. native/patches/vice-shim-runtime.patch is diagnostic legacy evidence only and is never applied.
